programme: EGR2 (Krox20), PAX3 and GBX2 form a developmental gene-regulatory axis that specifies and matures myelinating glia (EGR2 targets GJB1, MPZ, SOX10, ERBB2 — the canonical Schwann-cell/oligodendrocyte myelin regulon; PAX3 targets PDGFRA, the defining oligodendrocyte-precursor marker, plus FGFR1/MITF; GBX2 targets the hindbrain-patterning genes FGF8, WNT1, BMP4 that position glial progenitor domains). NR1H2 (LXR-beta) supplies the complementary lipid-handling arm needed to build myelin membrane, via its canonical cholesterol-efflux regulon (ABCA1, ABCG1, APOE, SREBF1, DHCR24, LPL).
role_in_a: In Huntington's disease, EGR2 appears in transcriptomic hub-gene analyses (shared with brain ischemia signatures), consistent with the broader, separately documented loss of oligodendrocyte maturation and myelin/cholesterol gene expression in HD white matter — but the retrieved record itself only shows EGR2 as a dysregulated hub gene, not an explicit myelination mechanism in HD, and PAX3/GBX2/NR1H2 carry no disease-specific literature hit in HD here.
role_in_b: In multiple sclerosis, PAX3- and GBX2-marked programmes generate the glial-restricted/oligodendrocyte progenitors that remyelinate lesions, EGR2 is active in microglia during demyelination, and NR1H2 (LXR-beta) drives the cholesterol-efflux machinery needed to rebuild myelin membrane after loss — together spanning the glial-specification-plus-lipid-supply axis that underlies remyelination, MS's core reparative bottleneck.
shared_axis: Both diseases separately involve impaired myelinating-glia function and CNS lipid handling — definitionally for MS as a demyelinating disease, and independently documented for HD's white-matter/oligodendrocyte pathology — so a shared transcriptional programme that specifies glial lineage (EGR2/PAX3/GBX2) and supplies the cholesterol needed to build myelin (NR1H2) would be expected to recur as concordant across patient groups in both, even without any single study examining the two diseases jointly.
reasoning: The module is genuinely nameable from the target genes alone (myelin structural genes for EGR2, the OPC marker PDGFRA for PAX3, hindbrain glial-patterning genes for GBX2, the LXR cholesterol regulon for NR1H2), and three of the four carrying factors are each placed by a retrieved paper in developmental/glial biology relevant to MS or in HD transcriptomic studies. But no retrieved source ties the programme to both diseases together, PAX3/GBX2's MS relevance is inferred from developmental-biology papers rather than clinical MS studies, and NR1H2 has no literature hit at all here (only elevated Open Targets percentiles in both diseases) — so the cross-disease bridge rests on reasoning, capping this at moderate rather than strong.
support: PMID 33875290 — EGR2 identified in a shared HD/brain-ischemia transcriptomic signature; PMID 31912694 — EGR2 flagged as a hub gene in HD bioinformatic analysis; PMID 42319825 — EGR2 active in microglia during demyelination in a mouse model, a chromatin-remodeling study framed around MS-relevant inflammation; PMID 21710609 — PAX3-marked dorsal spinal cord oligodendrocytes contribute to developmental axonal myelination, relevant to MS remyelination biology; PMID 30880587 — GBX2 used to generate hindbrain-specific glial-restricted progenitor cells, discussed in the context of multiple sclerosis.
how_to_falsify: In matched HD and MS brain (or induced-oligodendrocyte) samples, test whether EGR2, PAX3, GBX2 and NR1H2 targets (SOX10, MPZ, GJB1, PDGFRA, ABCA1, ABCG1, APOE) are co-regulated specifically within the oligodendrocyte-lineage compartment, and whether these four TFs show altered expression or binding in HD oligodendrocytes (not just in the immune/blood-derived samples that dominate the HD cohorts here). If the target genes move independently of each other, or if the HD signal for EGR2 traces to non-glial cell types, the shared myelin-biogenesis account does not hold and an immune/blood-driven explanation should be preferred instead.
caveats: Evidence spans blood and brain tissue across 6 independent cohort pairs and 546 patient-group comparisons; NFAT5 and PITX1 matched or exceeded the carrying factors' concordance (300/546) but were excluded here because their target profiles (osmotic-stress/immune activation for NFAT5, pituitary-hormone axis for PITX1) do not integrate into a myelin-biogenesis module — high recurrence alone was not treated as sufficient. The tissue-generic exclusion list is dominated by classic immune/MHC transcription factors (STAT1, CIITA, RFX5, IKZF1), confirming an immune-inflammatory story was deliberately stripped out before ranking, which is why this account rests on a developmental/lipid myelin axis rather than an immune one. NR1H2's placement is the weakest leg of the four, resting only on Open Targets association percentile (0.80 in HD, 0.98 in MS) with no supporting paper. ARID1A, YBX1, JUN, BRD4, SPDEF and EGR1 were retrieved but returned no evidence specific enough to place them in this or any other programme for either disease.
